text: The pragmatic photonic activation is opto-electronic (O-E-O). Why is its overhead acceptable?
choices: Because O-E-O conversion is completely energy-free
Because all-optical activations are actually cheaper per event
Because activations are O(N) while the matrix multiply is O(N^2), so the ~0.5-5 pJ, ~100 ps O-E-O cost per neuron is negligible at large N, and O-E-O also restores signal levels and gain
Because photons interact strongly, making electronic conversion unnecessary
explanation: The optics does the O(N^2) matrix work while O-E-O crossings scale only as O(N), so their per-neuron cost becomes asymptotically negligible at large N, and O-E-O supplies the gain and cascadability all-optical schemes lack. O-E-O is not energy-free (option 0), the point is scaling rather than per-event cost (option 1), and photons famously do NOT interact strongly (option 3).
